title: Rental contracts that renew automatically
detail: Standard rental contracts with automatic renewal (*prórroga automática*), for stability for tenants and small landlords. No length or terms are given.
c: Automatic renewal already exists (5–7 years under the 2019 law); extending it is realistic by ordinary law, but there are no parameters.
pos: Stability for tenants: fewer moves and fewer price jumps at renewal.
neg: Landlords lose flexibility and may leave long-term rental.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 7/2019 on rentals: contracts extended to 5–7 years (BOE)

title: Ban speculative home purchases
detail: Ban home purchases by commercial companies, investment funds and large owners. Large foreign buyers would need to have been on the local register (*padrón*) for at least 2 years and use the home as a main residence or let it at a regulated rent. Whole buildings could only be bought for regulated rental.
c: A general ban on companies buying homes breaches arts. 33 and 38 of the Constitution and EU free movement of capital.

title: Cap annual rent rises at 2%
detail: A permanent 2% cap on annual rent increases whenever yearly inflation (*IPC*) is higher. Tax deductions would be lost for any rise above the previous contract or the index limit.
c: A 2–3% indexation cap already applied in 2022–24. A permanent cap interferes with contracts; with high inflation, owners would leave the rental market.
pos: Protects tenants from inflation spikes, as the 2022–2024 cap did.
neg: A permanent cap below inflation cuts landlords' real income: an incentive to sell or switch to seasonal lets.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 6/2022: 2% cap on rent updates (BOE)
Ley 12/2023 on the right to housing (BOE)

title: Crack down on illegal tourist flats
detail: Re-table the bill barring platforms from advertising and booking illegal tourist flats (*vivienda turística*), which Congress accepted for debate but then stalled; 21% VAT on short tourist lets; state funding for towns with declared stressed areas.
c: A ban on advertising illegal flats is compatible with the 2024 EU short-term rental regulation, and realistic.
pos: Fewer illegal tourist flats and more homes for residents.
neg: Platforms will dispute it under EU law; an advertising ban also hits small owners who have not yet got a licence.

s.t: Regulation (EU) 2024/1028 on short-term rental data (BOE copy of the OJEU)

title: Bring back the energy levy; tax banks and large fortunes
detail: Restore and make permanent the levy on energy companies (*gravamen energético*) that PNV, PP, Vox, UPN and Junts voted down, collected by the Basque and Navarrese tax offices (*Haciendas Forales*). Raise taxes on banks and large fortunes; no amounts given.
c: Congress did not approve the energy levy in January 2025 (165 for, 183 against); it cannot be repeated without votes from the right and some nationalist parties.
pos: More revenue from companies with windfall profits and from the wealthy.
neg: A levy on energy firms may reduce their investment in grids and renewables; a bank tax is passed on to customers.

s.t: BOE, 23 Jan 2025: Congress did not approve RDL 10/2024 on the energy levy

title: 32-hour week with no pay cut
detail: Cut working time to 32 hours a week or four working days, with no pay cut, by reforming the Workers' Statute (*Estatuto de los Trabajadores*). Small and medium firms would start at 35 hours and reach the goal within three years.
c: As with Sumar and Podemos: even 37.5 hours did not pass in 2025.

s.t: Congress, BOCG 15-A-58-3: 37.5-hour bill returned to the government (10 Sep 2025)

title: Regularisation and a new immigration law
detail: Effective, accessible and stable regularisation (*regularización*) that issues residence and work permits and prevents people from falling back into irregular status; a new immigration law based on human rights. No dates, criteria or numbers.
c: As with Sumar: a permanent regularisation needs an organic law, and PP and Vox are against.
pos: Fewer people in the shadow economy: more tax and contributions.
neg: A permanent route may strengthen the "pull effect" (evidence on its size is disputed), and puts heavy pressure on offices, as in the 2026 regularisation (1.17 million applications).

s.t: La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026: 1,174,978 regularisation applications filed
